question.problem:
Consider the following predicates:

$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $x$ is prime $\qquad$ $Q(x):$ $x$ is not a multiple of $10$

Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)?$

- $x$ is not a multiple of $10$ if $x$ is prime

- If $x$ is not a multiple of $10,$ then $x$ is prime

- $x$ is prime implies $x$ is not a multiple of $10$

- $x$ is not a multiple of $10$ only if $x$ is prime
question.worked_solution:
Let's recall the following grammatical constructions for the implication $P\Rightarrow Q{:}$

- If $P,$ then $Q$

- $P$ only if $Q$

- $Q$ if $P$

- $P$ implies $Q$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

- Option I reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14123494/assets/482e156a7d3aef3f75a6b51efec5069fc48696749d7f580d4e40d7801a41f90a.svg)
which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{green}\checkmark}$

- Option II reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14123494/assets/fb19cec758144f4ae3ca6580d5171757369a831f6cfc7d940fa95fcfaf2522b9.svg)
which corresponds to $Q(x) \Rightarrow P(x).$ $\:{\color{red}\times}$

- Option III reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14123494/assets/1f472c122fe745e97fb31328625eccb71515dfee4b99e4bba548bf367cc8cc78.svg)
which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{darkgreen}\checkmark}$

- Option IV reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14123494/assets/525a046232143aa333ded66fb2bec55ff0011a8f76ef74373b9c6c99abdc3fd3.svg)
which corresponds to $Q(x) \Rightarrow P(x).$ $\:{\color{red}\times}$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
